validated_work_order.understanding: A custom report's conditions button is icon-only: CompactFiltersButton renders a bare Button whose only child is SvgFilter, with no text node and no aria-label, so its accessible name is empty. The e2e page model works around that by enumerating every button in the reports page, skipping any with an aria-label or non-empty text, and clicking the first one whose bounding box sits right of x=850 (custom-report-page.ts:openConditionsMenu). That is the only way the suite reaches the conditions menu, and it is why four call sites in reports.test.ts each carry their own copy of selectOnlyBillsGroup and switchToAnyOf. The fix is to give the button a name and to locate it by that name. This is the second planning pass; both objections from the rejected plan are answered in the fields below.
validated_work_order.root_cause: The control has no accessible name, and the locator that had to compensate for that compensates with geometry. The x>850 threshold is a function of the fixed-width content to the button's left, not of viewport width: ReportTopbar renders nine GraphButtons, three 1px dividers and a SnapshotButton, all flexShrink: 0, then a SpaceBetween with flex:1 and justifyContent:'space-between' (ReportTopbar.tsx:227-233) whose first child is the compact FilterButton. Inside a space-between row the first child sits at the region's left edge, so narrowing the window pushes SaveReport right rather than moving the filter button left - the reviewer is right that the old claim (the scan fails at 1024px) does not follow from the code. What does follow is that 850 is a fragile sum of sidebar widths (ReportSidebar minWidth 225, SidebarShell MIN_SIDEBAR_WIDTH 200) with little slack, and that a control with no name cannot be addressed at all except by such a sum.
validated_work_order.approach: Add aria-label={t('Filters')} to the existing bare Button in CompactFiltersButton, reusing the translation key the sibling tooltip already uses (FiltersMenu.tsx:744) and matching the pattern every other icon-only control in the topbar uses (GraphButton.tsx:42, SnapshotButton.tsx:45). An aria-label adds no rendered node, so no VRT snapshot moves. Then reduce openConditionsMenu to a single getByRole('button', { name: 'Filters', exact: true }).click(), which deletes the button scan, the hasName probe, the boundingBox call, the x>850 comparison and the now-unreachable throw, and hoist the two duplicated e2e helpers to the body of the 'custom reports' describe. Because no CI-executed check touches packages/desktop-client/e2e/ (config.yml has e2e: "", vitest includes only src/**, desktop-client tsconfig excludes e2e), the e2e suite is not a gate and is treated throughout as a local-only run in qa_script; the CI-executed backing for the accessible name is a new unit test under src/, and the page-model and suite criteria are stated as structural properties checkable by reading, never as a suite nobody runs.

files.change: Import useTranslation from 'react-i18next' (after the existing React import, matching FiltersMenu.tsx), call const { t } = useTranslation(); at the top of CompactFiltersButton, and pass aria-label={t('Filters')} to the existing <Button variant="bare" onPress={onPress} style={{ minWidth: 20 }}>. Nothing else changes: the SvgFilter child, the minWidth, the bare variant and the onPress plumbing stay exactly as they are, and no text node is introduced.
files.why: This is the root of the ticket. 'Filters' is already a translation key in this feature (the tooltip content at FiltersMenu.tsx:744), so no new string enters the catalog and `yarn generate:i18n` output is unaffected. aria-label rather than a visually-hidden span or a title attribute, because aria-label is the pattern already used by the neighbouring icon-only toolbar buttons and adds no DOM node, hence no layout shift and no VRT movement.

files.change: Replace the entire body of openConditionsMenu with one statement: await this.pageContent.getByRole('button', { name: 'Filters', exact: true }).click();. Delete the buttons/count loop, the hasName probe, the boundingBox() call, the box.x > 850 comparison and the unreachable throw. Rewrite the JSDoc to say the button is addressed by its accessible name rather than by its position among the topbar buttons. Keep the method name, signature and pageContent receiver - reports.test.ts calls it at :291 and :458 and this is its only definition.
files.why: Once the control has a name, the geometric scan is not just fragile but actively harmful: it skips every named button, so it would silently pick a different control the moment the toolbar gains any named button. exact:true is required because Playwright's default name matching is substring-based and the accounts page's non-compact sibling is named 'Filter' (FiltersButton.tsx:13, used at account-page.ts:56) - a substring match on 'Filters' would be fine, but exact:true keeps the two variants distinguishable.

files.change: Hoist the two duplicated helpers into the body of test.describe('custom reports', ...) immediately after its beforeEach and above the first nested describe: selectOnlyBillsGroup, taking the :479 copy and keeping its `/** Tick only the Bills group, as QA's T-9 does. */` comment; and switchToAnyOf, taking the :343 copy and keeping the two inline lines explaining that the toggle renders only once two or more conditions exist. Delete the byte-identical copies at :311-328, :479-496 (selectOnlyBillsGroup) and :343-352, :501-506 (switchToAnyOf). Leave all six call sites (:368, :374, :399, :422, :561, :563) untouched, and leave the single-copy helpers applyNotesFilter :290, waitForRows :333 and applyCategoryContains :457 where they are. Then add one test at the end of the 'custom reports' describe: await page.setViewportSize({ width: 1024, height: 720 }) inside a try, run selectMode('total') and selectViz('Data Table'), call openConditionsMenu(), assert await page.getByTestId('filters-select-tooltip') is visible, and restore the viewport with page.setViewportSize({ width: 1280, height: 720 }) in a finally.
files.why: The duplication is what made openConditionsMenu's four callers expensive to fix - each one carried private copies of the two helpers, so the same edit had to be reasoned about in four places. The new test exists because IAC-6 asks for the suite to hold at a narrower width, and it is described as what it is: a positive assertion that the role-and-name locator resolves at 1024px. It is green before and after this change and is not claimed as a regression test for the old scan. It goes last in the describe and restores the viewport in a finally because the enclosing 'Reports' describe is mode: 'serial' and contains toMatchThemeScreenshots cases, whose snapshots are captured at Playwright's 1280x720 default.

alternatives_considered.approach: Give the button a visually hidden text node instead of an aria-label (a <Text> with a screen-reader-only style).
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It adds a DOM node to a bare button with an explicit minWidth: 20, which is the kind of thing that moves pixels and invalidates visual-regression snapshots for no accessibility gain over aria-label. aria-label is what the neighbouring GraphButton and SnapshotButton already do.

alternatives_considered.approach: Keep the positional scan but widen or recompute the threshold, or scan for the button next to a known landmark.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It leaves the control without an accessible name, which is the actual defect: the button is announced to a screen reader as just "button". Fixing the locator instead of the name treats the symptom.

alternatives_considered.approach: Add a data-testid to CompactFiltersButton and point the page model at it.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It leaves the accessible name empty. The repo's convention for icon-only toolbar controls is aria-label (GraphButton.tsx:42, SnapshotButton.tsx:45), and there are already established name-based e2e locators (account-page.ts:56).

alternatives_considered.approach: Turn on an e2e check in .sdlc/config.yml so AC-4 and AC-6 become gate-verifiable as written.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: .sdlc/** is a path no ticket may change regardless of forbidden_paths. Restated as a route_request instead of done here.

assumptions: t('Filters') returns the literal string 'Filters' under the desktop-client vitest environment, because TestProviders (src/mocks.tsx:42) supplies no I18nextProvider and react-i18next falls back to the key. Supported by the existing FiltersMenu.test.tsx assertions, which match literal English produced from <Trans> children in the same environment.
The dev server used by Playwright runs in English; the suite already asserts literal English strings.

'Filters' is a better name than the sibling's singular 'Filter' because the control opens a list of filters and because the tooltip on this very control already says 'Filters' - introducing a second string would mean a second key for one button.
unknowns: Whether the old x>850 scan actually failed at any narrower width. It does not follow from the source: the button is the first child of a flex:1 space-between SpaceBetween (ReportTopbar.tsx:227-234), so its left edge is fixed by the flexShrink:0 siblings to its left, and narrowing the window moves SaveReport right rather than the filter button left. Relatedly, isNarrowWidth is width < 512 (tokens.ts small: 512) and gates the whole ReportTopbar at CustomReport.tsx:930, so a genuinely narrow width removes the button instead of relocating it. Verifying either would need a checkout with node_modules and a browser; until then the new 1024px case is claimed only as a positive assertion that the locator resolves by role and name.

Whether the VRT snapshots in reports.test.ts are byte-identical after adding an aria-label. They should be - aria-label renders nothing - but only a local `yarn workspace @actual-app/web run vrt` confirms it, and VRT is not a CI gate either.
validated_work_order.debate_summary: No debate: this is a single-agent planning pass on the second attempt, with no other agents reporting. Both objections from the rejected plan are answered directly in the plan. Objection 1 (AC-4 and AC-6 unverifiable by CI) is real - no CI-executed check touches packages/desktop-client/e2e/ - and the reviewer's option (a), enabling an e2e check, is unavailable to me because .sdlc/config.yml is a path no ticket may change; option (b) is taken instead, restating both criteria as structural properties checkable by reading and backing the accessible name itself with a src/ unit test that `yarn test` runs, with the Playwright run demoted to qa_script and risks as explicitly local-only. Objection 2 (the 1024px claim contradicted by unknowns) is also upheld: the source shows the filter button pinned to the left edge of a flex:1 space-between region, so the old scan's threshold is a function of sidebar widths rather than viewport width, and isNarrowWidth below 512px removes the topbar entirely. The 'fails today' claim is dropped rather than re-argued, and the new e2e case is described as the positive assertion it is.

route_request.reason: The reviewer's first objection cannot be fully discharged inside this ticket: .sdlc/config.yml sets e2e: "" while CI's only check over packages/desktop-client/e2e/ is lint, so no e2e criterion can be gate-verifiable without editing .sdlc/**, a path no ticket may change. This plan works around it by restating AC-4 and AC-6 as structural properties and backing the accessible name with a src/ unit test, but if the intent is for the e2e suite to gate merges, that is a config change belonging to a maintainer decision before the work lands, not a plan detail.
